overlap.interpretation_very_high: Nearly identical tag targeting. Both videos are competing directly for the same audience and search queries. Your unique tags are your main differentiator.
overlap.interpretation_high: Strong topical alignment. Both videos target the same niche and share most of the core discovery tags.
overlap.interpretation_moderate: Related content with partial tag strategy overlap. You're in the same niche but targeting different segments of it.
overlap.interpretation_low: Minimal shared targeting despite being in the same content space. Either very different sub-niches or very different tag strategies.
overlap.interpretation_very_low: Almost no shared tag strategy. These videos are in very different territory despite appearing similar on the surface.
overlap.recommendation_very_high: Focus on the tags you have that they don't — these are your competitive edges. Consider diversifying your strategy to reduce direct competition.
overlap.recommendation_high: Add the missing tags to compete more directly. The competitor's unique tags show angles you haven't covered.
overlap.recommendation_moderate: The missing tags represent an opportunity to expand your audience reach into the segments this competitor is capturing.
overlap.recommendation_low: Study the competitor's complete tag set carefully. The large gap suggests they may be targeting search terms you haven't discovered yet.
overlap.recommendation_very_low: Consider whether this is truly a direct competitor, or whether their tag strategy could be adopted wholesale to access a different audience segment.

faq.section_sub: Everything you need to know about YouTube tag extraction, thumbnail downloading, and creator SEO.
faq.q1: What are YouTube tags and do they still matter for SEO?
faq.a1: YouTube tags are keywords you add to a video to help YouTube understand its topic. While tags carry less weight than they did several years ago, they still contribute to how YouTube categorises your content — especially for searches where the tag matches the query exactly. They are one signal among many, including the title, description, and viewer engagement. Most successful creators still use tags strategically, particularly long-tail phrases (3+ words) that match specific search intent.
faq.q2: What is the YouTube tag character limit?
faq.a2: YouTube enforces a 500-character limit on the combined length of all tags for a video, including the separators between them. Tags are counted as a single comma-separated string. When you exceed this limit, YouTube silently truncates tags from the end of your list — the excess tags are simply ignored without any warning. ytspy's character counter shows exactly how much budget a video has used and highlights any tags that would be cut off.
faq.q3: Can I extract tags from any YouTube video?
faq.a3: You can extract tags from any public YouTube video where the creator has added tags. Age-restricted videos, private videos, and members-only videos cannot be accessed without authentication, so tag data is unavailable for those. Some creators choose not to add tags at all — in that case ytspy will still show thumbnails and metadata, but the tag list will be empty. YouTube Shorts are also supported.
faq.q4: What is the difference between short-tail, mid-tail, and long-tail tags?
faq.a4: Short-tail tags are single words (e.g. 'gaming'). They are broad, high-traffic, and extremely competitive. Mid-tail tags are two words (e.g. 'gaming tips'). They balance reach with specificity. Long-tail tags are three or more words (e.g. 'how to improve aim in FPS games'). They are highly specific, face less competition, and often convert better because they match precise search intent. The optimal tag strategy uses a mix of all three types, weighted toward long-tail.
faq.q5: How do I download YouTube thumbnails in the highest quality?
faq.a5: ytspy provides thumbnails in five resolutions: 1280×720 (Max resolution), 640×480 (Standard), 480×360 (High quality), 320×180 (Medium quality), and WebP format. The 1280×720 resolution is available for most videos but not all — older videos or videos without custom thumbnails may only have lower resolutions. The download is handled as a direct file download — no right-click required.
faq.q6: What is the tag health score?
faq.a6: The tag health score is a 0–100 composite rating of how well a video's tag strategy is optimised. It measures four things: budget efficiency (how well the 500-character budget is used), tail distribution (how balanced the mix of short, mid, and long-tail tags is), word diversity (how varied the vocabulary across tags is), and hashtag alignment (whether the description hashtags also appear as tags). A score above 86 is excellent. The breakdown explains exactly what to improve.
faq.q7: How does the bulk extraction feature work?
faq.a7: Paste up to 10 YouTube URLs into the bulk textarea, one per line. ytspy fetches them in parallel batches and returns all tags, a frequency table showing which tags appear across multiple videos, per-video health scores, and a one-click ZIP download of all thumbnails. The frequency table highlights which tags are common across the niche — these are high-competition niche tags. You can also download the complete results as a CSV for use in spreadsheets.
faq.q8: How do I analyse competitor tags?
faq.a8: Use the Competitor tag analysis section. Paste your video URL and a competitor's URL. ytspy extracts both tag lists and shows you three columns: tags both videos share, tags the competitor has that you don't, and your unique tags. The missing column is sorted by estimated SEO value — long-tail tags first. A single button copies all missing tags in YouTube-ready format so you can paste them directly into YouTube Studio.
faq.q9: Does ytspy work with YouTube Shorts?
faq.a9: Yes. YouTube Shorts URLs (youtube.com/shorts/VIDEO_ID) are fully supported. ytspy normalises them to the equivalent watch page before extraction. Shorts thumbnails are displayed in the appropriate vertical preview contexts. Note that some Shorts may have limited metadata since they are a different content format from regular videos.
faq.q10: Is ytspy free? Are there any limits?
faq.a10: ytspy is completely free with no account required. There are no daily limits on single extractions. The bulk mode processes up to 10 videos per run, which is a practical limit rather than an artificial one. The tool runs on serverless infrastructure with a rate limit of 15 requests per minute per IP address to prevent abuse — this would only affect automated scripts, not regular use.
faq.q11: What is the tag template library?
faq.a11: The template library lets you save named sets of tags for future use. After extracting a video you frequently tag similarly — a podcast episode, a tutorial in an ongoing series, or a product review in a consistent niche — you can save its tags as a named template. When uploading a new video, you can apply any saved template with one click, choosing whether to add to existing tags, replace them, or put the template tags first. Templates are stored in your browser and never leave your device.
faq.q12: Why does the multi-placement thumbnail preview matter?
faq.a12: YouTube thumbnails appear in five distinct contexts — desktop homepage, desktop search, mobile search, suggested video sidebar, and bell notification — each rendering at a different size. A thumbnail that looks excellent at full resolution can be unreadable at 48×48 pixels, which is the size of a notification icon. Text-heavy thumbnails in particular often fail at small sizes. ytspy shows all five contexts simultaneously so you can evaluate whether your thumbnail communicates clearly at every scale before uploading.

quick_answer.label: QUICK ANSWER
quick_answer.text: YouTube tags are hidden keywords embedded in a video's source code. ytspy extracts them from any public YouTube video, shows you competitor tags you're missing, and scores your tag strategy — all free, with no login required.

logic.label: LOGIC
logic.text: YouTube embeds all video metadata including tags inside a JavaScript object called ytInitialData in every public video page — no API key required.

methodology.label: METHODOLOGY
methodology.text: ytspy uses a 4-layer server-side extraction chain with automatic fallback, returning only structured JSON — never raw HTML — to the browser.

seo_content.p_how_works: Every public YouTube video embeds its tags in the page source code. ytspy fetches that page server-side, extracts all metadata from the ytInitialData JavaScript object, and returns clean structured data — no API key required, no rate limits for end users.
seo_content.h2_char_limit: What is the YouTube tag character limit?
seo_content.p_char_limit: YouTube enforces a 500-character limit on the total combined length of all tags for a video, including separators. Most creators don't know they've exceeded this limit until tags are silently truncated. The character counter on ytspy shows exactly how much of the 500-character budget any video has used.
seo_content.p_bulk_zip: Downloading thumbnails for multiple YouTube videos one at a time is slow. ytspy lets you paste up to 10 URLs and download all thumbnails as a single ZIP file with one click — no server upload required, the ZIP is assembled entirely in your browser.
seo_content.h2_competitor: YouTube tag gap analysis — free competitor research
seo_content.p_competitor: Understanding which tags your competitors use that you don't is one of the highest-leverage actions in YouTube SEO. ytspy shows the exact tag gap between your video and any competitor video, highlighting the tags most likely to help your discovery.
